changes: p2 Indrānanda: removed 'owner' — the colophon says only that the copy was written and given to him (-yāta ... viyā); kept 'beneficiary'
p3 Toraṇānanda: added 'donor' because 'coyājo viyā jula' means 'wrote and gave'
date: month normalised to vaiśākha (written vaiśāṣa); weekday glossed as Tuesday; era NS is an inference, recorded in notes

purpose: written by Toraṇānanda and given to Indrānanda (śrīindrānaṃdayāta ... coyājo viyā jula)
notes: The era is not named ('śubhasamvat'). I read it as Nepāla Saṃvat (NS) because the colophon is in Newari and has the '-miti' formula. That gives 1891 CE, which fits a late Devanagari paper copy of the Buddhacarita (the Nepalese Buddhacarita manuscripts are 19th-century copies). The weekday was not verified against an ephemeris. 'viyā' (gave) shows the copy was a gift from the scribe to Indrānanda. The two men are not said to be related.
